issues.failure_explanation: In the alpha=4 proof, the error on each subinterval J_m is bounded by c*Err_{m-1} + c*tau^{1/2} + c*T_1^{1/2}*Err_m. The proof then replaces c*T_1^{1/2}*Err_m by (1/2)*Err_m so that this term can be absorbed. The choice T_1 <= c^{-2} only gives c*T_1^{1/2} <= 1. With equality allowed, the inequality reads Err_m <= ... + Err_m and yields no bound. Absorption needs T_1 <= (2c)^{-2}. The recursion Err_m <= 2c(Err_{m-1}+tau^{1/2}), the absolute bound (ErrAbsNew) and the constants C, L, tau_0 are all built on this step, so the stated derivation does not follow as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define T_1 := min{T, b_0, (2c)^{-2}}, so that c*T_1^{1/2} <= 1/2. Keep L = ceil(2T/T_1) and re-define C and tau_0 accordingly. The rest of the iteration, rates and scope are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The alpha=4 case of Theorem ThmStrang, in both norms, is not established by the argument as written. The fully discrete alpha=4 bound in ThmStrangFully is finished 'as in the semi-discrete case' and inherits the same step. The result itself is not threatened, only the constant bookkeeping.
issues.title: Interval length T_1 in the alpha=4 iteration does not give the claimed absorption factor 1/2
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line change of a constant in the definition of T_1, with L, C and tau_0 following mechanically. No new lemma or argument is required, and all rates and claims survive.
